target_customer: Developers and companies running open weight AI models via API and agent sandboxes (current website); the original YC listing describes AI apps for Southeast Asian enterprises and consumers
problem: Running open models and agent sandboxes is costly and slow; the original Latent Space listing targeted AI apps for emerging economies.
business_model: Usage-based API with pay as you go and subscription plans
product_category: Open model inference API and agent sandboxes

technical_complexity.rationale: Original AI concierge and visa apps were standard app engineering in 2022; the current inference business has harder infrastructure work.

defensibility.rationale: Application layer products and inference resale are easy to copy.

market_need_then: No sourced evidence of demand at founding was found beyond the company description of AI apps for emerging economies.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and slightly playful developer copy (company site)

rebrands.why: Not stated; the YC listing text still describes Latent Space while the site is OpenScale built by LatentSpace

brand_strength.rationale: No sources about the brand itself; identity split between Latent Space and OpenScale.

pivots.from: AI apps for Southeast Asian enterprises and consumers (Halo AI, GoVisa, Supa)
pivots.to: Open model inference API and agent sandboxes (OpenScale)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the YC listing versus the current website

outcome_analysis: The sources do not show a funding history or outcome. The YC listing describes the earlier Latent Space apps while the live website sells an open model API and sandboxes under the OpenScale name, which suggests a later pivot whose date and reason are not public.
notes: The YC page mixes Latent Space details with OpenScale. A $1.8M seed in 2026 belongs to a different company, SPUN, not this one. No dated competitor sources near the 2022 batch were found, so the list is empty. Several searches found nothing on an outcome.
